Hi! I’m Kabir. I live in Jaipur, in India. I love going to school because I learn new things there every day. I wear a watch to school because I want to be on time for my lessons. But people didn’t always have watches, clocks and mobile phones to tell the time. They used sundials!

The first sundials were easy to make. People used stones or drew lines on the ground to show the hours. Then they put a stick in the ground, and the shadow of the stick told the time. Hello! My name is Zakia. I’m from Java in Indonesia, and I love eating chocolate! You need cocoa beans and sugar to make chocolate. They both grow on farms in Indonesia.

People didn’t always have cocoa in Indonesia. Cocoa first grew in Central and South America. The people there made a drink from cocoa beans mixed with hot water. Sometimes they added honey and spices to the drink. They put cocoa in their food, too.

When Europeans visited Central and South America, they liked the cocoa drink, so they took cocoa beans back with them to Europe. Then, in Europe, they learnt to make chocolate from cocoa. Hello! My name is Rachid and I’m from Alnif, in Morocco. My hobby is collecting fossils. Fossils are parts of animals and plants that lived millions of years ago. The bodies of these animals and plants, or prints of their bodies, are preserved in rocks. For example, fossils can be pieces of trees and plants or shark’s teeth. Alnif is a great place to find fossils. I have got a fossilised shark’s tooth. I’ve also got lots of trilobites and ammonites – two kinds of sea animals that lived millions of years ago, when this part of Morocco was under the sea. One day I want to find a fossil of a dinosaur.

Yesterday, I read in a book about how some fossils are made. Long ago, when animals died, their bodies sometimes fell into mud or sand at the bottom of a river, and they sank into the mud or the sand. The soft parts of their bodies rotted and only their skeleons were left.

With time, the mud or the sand pressed down on their skeletons, and their bones, teeth and shells got harder and harder. Slowly, the sand turned into rock. The parts of the animals stayed in the rock, and today we find their fossils.

Sometimes we find lots of fossils of fish and sea animals deep in the ground. This tells us that the place was under water long ago. So fossils help us to understand our world.
